title: Application-core feature streams exiting early
first_prompt:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

<system-reminder>
<tools-used-before-summary>Ag

commits.summary: example-targets positive: the three positive packets source-locked (305, 306, 307)
commits.body:
New real-world examples 305 (Spring Boot e8de5a6d, the Outcome enum behind WebMvcTags.outcome), 306 (Spring Framework db9a10bf, PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch's prefix check as startsWith) and 307 (Spring Security fe9e4549, BCrypt.hashpw with StandardCharsets.UTF_8), the positive stream's P1-P3 of llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md. Each has example.json, a target.json sidecar (identity, history, preparation route, named tasks with native strict engines and expected outcomes, handoff), a sources.lock.json and a README. No build, replay or proof ran; claim files, oracles, drivers, probes and mutants come next.

Every commit and parent was checked against github.com by a shallow fetch by SHA (all single-parent), and the selected source files' git blob ids were recorded beside the nearest releases'. That check contradicts the stream brief's statement that these pairs have no published JARs and take the upstream build route: 306's PatternMatchUtils.java is byte-identical at 27bfcbbc/v5.3.6 and db9a10bf/v5.3.7 and in Maven Central's spring-core 5.3.6 and 5.3.7 sources JARs, so 306 uses the published-artifact route with pinned sha256s (fetched by hand, sha1s matching Central's). 305's exact-commit Maven build is predicted irreproducible, because both commits pin SNAPSHOT and milestone dependencies; 307's Gradle build needs services.gradle.org and repo.spring.io, outside decision 1. Both are recorded as predicted build blockers, with the user's options under the brief's Progress, together with three interface requests for the merge (mutant revisions, the router index, companion links).

commits.summary: example-targets positive P2: 306's claim, oracle, driver, probes and dropped-prefix mutant
commits.body: Example 306 (Spring Framework db9a10bf, simpleMatch's prefix check rewritten as startsWith) now has a frozen claim and its concrete controls. claims/simple-match-preservation.json uses the claim format of workflow's W1 (example-target-claim/v1, not yet merged). Its domain: decision preservation over a pattern and a string, each null or at most 6 UTF-16 code units of any value (maxArrayLength 6, unwind 16), with the boolean and the exception observed. replay/probes.json has 40 probes: the brief's nine, the star shapes, a prefix mismatch, non-ASCII, a surrogate pair, half a pair and isolated surrogates. controls/oracle.py decides each glob independently, by dynamic programming over code units, and checks each revision's driver lines against that and against each other. replay/driver prints one JSON line per probe. controls/drop-prefix.patch is the mutant: release-after with the prefix condition dropped. target.json lists all four as controls and records two predicted blockers: seven JDK String methods the native checker approximates, and null String parameters.

commits.summary: example-targets positive P1: 305's claims, oracle, driver, probes and 200-boundary mutant
commits.body:
Example 305 (Spring Boot e8de5a6d, the Outcome enum behind WebMvcTags.outcome) gets the packet the positive brief's P1 asks for. Two claims in workflow W1's example-target-claim/v1 format:
- claims/outcome-preservation.json, for the preservation task: a null response, or a carrier whose getStatus() returns any int. It observes the tag's key and value by value, never identity, since the patch moves the tags' caching, and the exception.
- claims/finite-outcome.json, shared by finite-outcome-before and finite-outcome-after: key outcome, one of the six values, nothing thrown.
The rest of the packet:
- 27 probes: the brief's 15, negative statuses and codes past 599.
- An independent oracle that reads the status class from the status's decimal spelling (RFC 9110 section 15).
- A driver whose response is a Proxy carrier of HttpServletResponse; any method other than getStatus() throws.
- The mutant, controls/status-200.patch on after's Outcome.java: 200 becomes INFORMATIONAL.
target.json names the controls and records two more predicted blockers. The README records the enum, Tag, class-initialization and response-interface requirements, and how this positive's int input compares with the negative's method strings.

Verified by hand, as notes and not evidence, since neither side is the commits' build (the exact build pins SNAPSHOTs).
- The JARs are Central's (sha1 matched).
- Before's WebMvcTags.java was compiled from source into a copy of the 2.2.0.RELEASE actuator JAR. Its Framework dependency's HttpStatus.java is byte-identical at 5.2.0.RC2 and 5.2.0.RELEASE.
- Before agrees with after, compiled from source and as published, and with the oracle on all 27 probes, on JDK 21 and 25. The mutant differs at 200 only.
- A jvmcontract gaps scan (records/outcome-gaps.json) found Pattern.compile in WebMvcTags.<clinit> and Objects.requireNonNull in micrometer's ImmutableTag.<init> on both sides. So every strict attempt is predicted to be refused.
- W1's planner, run from a temp copy of wqsyopql, plans all four tasks.
- The targets suite (41), test_build (190), the contract (16, 13 skipped) and build.py --plan pass.
Progress also records, for the coordinator, the check's 'no manifest' errors on eight of other streams' changes.

The brief is out of date in one respect: P1 says the outcome tests are upstream's OutcomeTests, which is right, but the stream brief's starting-evidence claim that these pairs have no published JARs only half holds for P1. 2.2.0.RELEASE publishes after's WebMvcTags unchanged; before's has no artifact.

commits.summary: example-targets positive P3: 307's claim, oracle, driver, probes and US-ASCII mutant
commits.body:
Example 307 (Spring Security fe9e4549, BCrypt.hashpw(String,String) moving from getBytes("UTF-8") to getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) gets its packet. claims/hashpw-preservation.json, in workflow W1's example-target-claim/v1 format, freezes the domain. The password is null or at most 80 UTF-16 code units of any values. The salt is one of seven fixed strings from upstream's BCryptTests: the 'abc' test vector's cost-6 salt and its stored hash, the $2$05$ salt, and null, empty, cost-03 and too-short salts. The claim observes the returned String or the exception's class. The brief's three domain decisions are explicit: a null password (NullPointerException), malformed surrogates (encoded as '?', as String.getBytes specifies) and invalid salts (IllegalArgumentException) are all in the domain. Exception messages are excluded, because since JDK 14 an NPE's message names the method the patch changes.

replay/probes.json has 45 probes, among them 71, 72 and 73 UTF-8 bytes in 1- to 4-byte characters and a character straddling byte 72, plus three upstream known answers. controls/oracle.py computes no cipher. It encodes UTF-8 itself, and predicts that probes with the same salt and the same first 72 bytes of bcrypt's cyclic key share a result; that distinct keys give distinct results is a stated assumption. That makes the encoding observable, also against the stored hash. The driver passes arguments as UTF-16 code units. The mutant controls/us-ascii.patch (sha256 a2b4e97f...) is on after. target.json gains the claim, the controls and two predicted blockers (java-semantics, input-construction); README and example.json describe the packet.

Verified by hand, as notes, not evidence. Each commit's BCrypt.java was compiled alone with javac 8, and Central's spring-security-crypto 5.2.0.RELEASE (sha1 checked) was run beside them. All three agree with the oracle and with each other on all 45 probes, byte-identically on JDK 21 and 25. The mutant breaks the oracle 9 times and differs on 17 non-ASCII probes. javap shows before and after differ only in hashpw(String,String), apart from constant-pool indices. A jvmcontract gaps scan (records/hashpw-gaps.json) refuses the changed conversion itself on both sides (getBytes(String), getBytes(Charset), StandardCharsets.UTF_8), plus Arrays.copyOf, Integer.parseInt and StringBuilder.charAt in the callee. W1's planner, run from a temporary copy of wqsyopql, plans both tasks. The targets suite (41), test_build.py (190), the contract (16, 13 skipped) and build.py --plan pass. Progress names P5 (example 105) as next; the brief is otherwise accurate.

commits.summary: example-targets positive: propose upstream BCrypt test vectors for the allow list
commits.body: P3's commit warned about 15 long-token findings in this session's log. Each was checked with review show (masked): every one is an expected hash from the public test_vectors table of Spring Security's BCryptTests.java (blob dc242a49), printed while choosing example 307's fixed salt. That is published upstream test data, not a credential. Each is proposed with sync.py allow propose and stays a warning until the user approves it. Progress records this for the user, and brings the coordinator's list of cross-workspace 'no manifest' errors to eleven changes, all other streams'.

commits.summary: example-targets positive P5: 105 migrated, with its A5 obligation, oracle, driver, probes and the 105-109 inventory
commits.body:
Example 105 (apache/commons-numbers#223, ArithmeticUtils.pow) gets a target.json sidecar and its packet; its handwritten README, summary and verdict label stay as the historical report. Revisions were resolved afresh from github.com: before e7c172d2 (the squash merge's only parent), after 8cfc04e8 (the merge), and the pull request head 79aa4643, whose ArithmeticUtils.java is after's. Maven Central's commons-numbers-core 1.3 carries before's file and the same bytecode as that file compiled alone; no release carries after's, so the route is the upstream Maven build of each commit (JDK 11, Central only by its POMs), not yet run.

The selected obligation for gate A5 is claims/pow-minus-two.json: for k == -2 and 0 <= e <= 31, pow(int,int) returns (-2)^e. It is expected established on after and refuted on before at (-2, 31), under --engine native --gaps strict. A jvmcontract gaps scan (records/pow-gaps.json, a hand-run note) finds only the StringBuilder calls of the e < 0 message, which the assume excludes. The report's equivalence rows are kept as diagnostic tasks. regression is expected refuted. confined-change is expected established, but is predicted refused under strict at those gaps, and is recorded as a predicted blocker.

Verified: controls/oracle.py, written from the Javadoc alone, checks a hand replay of 75 probes through replay/driver. Each commit's file was compiled alone, plus the published 1.3 JAR, each run in its own JVM on JDK 21 and 25 (a note, not evidence). After meets the contract on every probe; before and 1.3 give identical output and deviate at (-2, 31) alone; the oracle fails, as it should, on the wrong revision's output and on a truncated file. The claims validate against W1's claim schema, the sidecar against sidecar.load, and W1's planner plans all five tasks. The targets suite (41), test_build (190), the contract (3 pass, 13 at stubs) and build.py --plan pass. records/legacy-inventory.json inventories 105-109 without touching 106-109. The stream's Progress now says its acceptance is met, Status: done.

commits.summary: example-targets positive: record the two new cross-workspace manifest errors for the coordinator
commits.body: P5's commit check reported 13 'session ... has no manifest' ERRORs, all on other streams' changes. Two are new since P3's commit: qyzrtrwr (the workflow session) and kwzmplxt (the negative session). The Progress entry for the coordinator now lists all thirteen. Nothing in this stream's files caused them, and nothing was changed for them; the 15 long-token warnings are the BCrypt test vectors already proposed for the allow list, now in more copies of this session's log.
